## Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding (DCCD) Paper

The paper was published as a preprint on March 5, 2026.

**What is DCCD?**

DCCD is a simple two-step, training-free inference procedure that decouples semantic planning from structural enforcement: an unconstrained draft is generated first, and constrained decoding is then applied, conditioned on this draft, to guarantee validity.

**The Problem it Solves:**

Large language models are increasingly used to generate executable outputs, JSON objects, and API calls, where a single syntax error can make the output unusable. Constrained decoding enforces validity token-by-token via masking and renormalization, but it can distort generation when the model assigns low probability mass to valid continuations, pushing decoding toward locally valid yet semantically incorrect trajectories.

**Key Results:**

DCCD improves strict structured accuracy by up to +24 percentage points over standard constrained decoding (e.g., 15.2% to 39.0% on GSM8K with a 1B model), and enables smaller model pairs to match or exceed much larger constrained baselines, yielding substantial gains in parameter efficiency.

**Authors and Source:**

The paper is by Avinash Reddy and 3 other authors, available on arXiv at 2603.03305. The code is also available at GitHub.

Boosted Constrained Decoding (BoostCD) trains a new model to predict the ground-truth output based on both the constrained and the unconstrained generation from the autoregressive base model together with the input text. Constrained decoding approaches allow specifying constraints in form of context-free grammars. Encoder-decoder models used for structure prediction for information extraction tasks in low-resource settings clearly benefit from grammar-constrained decoding guiding the output generation.

Recent work reduces constrained decoding for generalized code generation paradigms to an operation on formal languages, enabling constrained decoding for infilling and diffusion LLMs.

KnowCoder aims to develop a kind of unified schema representation that LLMs can easily understand and an effective learning framework that encourages LLMs to follow schemas and extract structured knowledge accurately.

## Overview

BoostCD is a new method for training autoregressive language models for structured NLP tasks. It is applied to closed information extraction (cIE) as an example of a structured task with constraints defined by the content of the knowledge base that tend to change dynamically in real-life settings.

## How BoostCD Works

The BoostCD pipeline combines constrained and unconstrained decoding in two phases: Phase 1 decodes from the base model twice, in constrained and unconstrained mode, obtaining two weak predictions. In phase 2, a learned autoregressive boosted model combines the two weak predictions into one final prediction. The mistakes made by the base model with vs. without constraints tend to be complementary, which the boosted model learns to exploit for improved performance.

## BoostIE Model

BoostCD is instantiated for the closed information extraction (cIE) task, obtaining a model termed BoostIE. BoostIE is further enhanced with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) for improving performance on out-of-distribution data.

## Results

BoostIE outperforms previous methods both in-distribution (on synthetic data it was trained on) and out-of-distribution (on random Wikipedia paragraphs), and also demonstrates that BoostIE lowers the rate of common errors made by earlier techniques.

## Key Findings

Code to reproduce all experiments is available at https://github.com/avinashreddydev/dccd.

### What is DCCD?

Draft-Conditioned Constrained Decoding (DCCD) is a simple two-step, training-free inference procedure that decouples semantic planning from structural enforcement: an unconstrained draft is generated first, and constrained decoding is then applied, conditioned on this draft, to guarantee validity.

### How It Works

In Step 1, a model generates an unconstrained draft that captures the semantic plan or intermediate reasoning. In Step 2, the final structured output is generated using constrained decoding conditioned on the draft.

### Performance

Across all model scales, DCCD achieves the best aggregated performance, with the largest relative gains for smaller models where hard constraints induce the strongest projection distortion.

The official GitHub repository for the DCCD implementation is at https://github.com/avinashreddydev/dccd, where you can find the code and resources to implement and reproduce the research.

## Overview

DCCD is a simple two-step, training-free inference procedure that decouples semantic planning from structural enforcement: an unconstrained draft is generated first, and constrained decoding is then applied, conditioned on this draft, to guarantee validity.

## Two-Step Procedure

**Step 1**: A model generates an unconstrained draft that captures the semantic plan or intermediate reasoning.

**Step 2**: The final structured output is generated using constrained decoding conditioned on the draft. Conditioning shifts probability mass toward schema-consistent continuations, so the subsequent constraint enforcement step is substantially less distortive.

## Efficiency Gains

Because Step 2 primarily performs structured realization rather than open-ended reasoning, it can often be carried out by the same model or a smaller projector model, improving parameter efficiency.

## Performance Results

Across structured reasoning benchmarks, DCCD improves strict structured accuracy by up to +24 percentage points over standard constrained decoding (e.g., 15.2% to 39.0% on GSM8K with a 1B model), and enables smaller model pairs to match or exceed much larger constrained baselines, yielding substantial gains in parameter efficiency.

## Code Repository

Code to reproduce all experiments is available at https://github.com/avinashreddydev/dccd.
